notes.title: Update on development and small Christmas Q&A with Infinity Area (in French)
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

I hope you're all doing well and that you survived this past year. 

The development for Derelicts has been going steady and I've been working a lot on optimization during the first semester, and focused a lot on rewriting code and cleaning up my project for the second part, so I can start the real world building and focus on the core gameplay mechanics. 

I'm really excited to start this phase as I'll have a lot more to show for in the coming months.

Together with Florian, a friend working on the website Infinity Area, we made a small written Q&A (that one was in French only so be sure to use your favorite translator) that you can find at the following link:

https://infinity-area.com/article/interview-exclusive-sur-le-jeu-derelicts-un-jeu-de-survie

I wish you all a Merry Christmas with family and friends.

I'll see you in 2025 with more content and updates!

Romain

notes.title: June News!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!👋 

I hope your week went well.

I know I've been quiet on the teasers and updates front for a while and I apologize- so much to do to have great foundations and optimize all my assets and gamepaly code for the game! I used the past months to prepared most of the optimization and be sure that the mold of the game will allow me to scale up some systems in an efficient way (building, AI, level design). I was focused on making the game run as well as possible, trying to target older builds as well as offering more recent techs for the newer ones (DLSS, FSR, Frame Generation, Xess).

The next weeks/months will be really exciting as I'll have a lot more to show in 2024 now that I'm entering the real "visual" part of building the game.

I just posted a news update to Patreon with more details, viewable by all, with some new images and other news-  so check it out! 

At the moment, I have removed the tiers as I'll be reworking them next week to offer some new ones that will be oriented on more exclusive news content (dev logs, screenshots, videos) additionally to the news I'll share for everyone on Steam and socials.

https://www.patreon.com/posts/june-news-update-106934035


I'll keep you posted very soon! 🍻 

Have a great weekend!

Romain

notes.title: Vestiges at dusk.
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

I hope you're all doing well.

I have been progressing a lot for the past month. I've been delayed on some of my mechanics that I wanted to polish and optimize a lot more, such as the building system. I'm trying to get a good performance while players can still build a thousand of stuff on screen. This is hard but really worth it in the long run.

It's also taking a lot longer to optimize the levels in an efficient way, so your GPU doesn't die while playing. My goal is that the game can run at least smoothly on former GPUS, without DLSS on, which is really a challenging part while trying to keep everything realistic. But I know I'll get there!

I've been playing a lot with Unreal Engine 5 features recently and will offer the choice to unable a lot of really performance-heavy options such as Nanite and Lumen for players who cannot afford more recent GPUs. But don't worry, all the recent techs will be there (DLSS 3, Ray Tracing, Nanite, Lumen).

Here are two really short sneak peeks at the beach and the water effect I've been working on for the past week.

Have a great week and enjoy playing other games in the meantime!

Romain

notes.title: I'm working on making the nights really dark...
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41803584/9f9d56fb79371519fa9327b7c03c1d89ed64179e.png[/img]

Hello everyone. I hope you are doing well.

Development has been really great the past weeks and I'm making a really good progress.

Recently, I've started to work on the map, choosing the right type of foliage (good-looking and as optimized as possible) and the right type of textures/materials in order to run the game the best way possible.

I've also been looking into Virtual Textures and they should drastically improve the framerate of the game as well if used!

Overall, a lot of work on optimization and choosing the right things before proceeding to build the full world!

I wish you a great week!

Romain

notes.title: A new friend...
notes.content:
Hello guys!
I hope you enjoyed your weekend.

I've recently been working on a new creepy enemy that will give you a good scare at night, crawling in the bushes!

I'm trying to add innovative ideas concerning foes and work a lot on their AI, to make them behave in a more interesting way than most survival games. My main model for this is The Forest, in which the AI is really well done and make the enemies work in groups or sometimes afraid of the players.
